sections.heading: Eligibility and timing
paragraphs: The Reserve Bank of India stated that SGB 2020-21 Series VII, issued on 20 October 2020, became eligible for premature redemption after the fifth year on an interest-payment date. Because 20 October 2026 was a holiday, the due date was 19 October 2026.
The mechanism is conditional rather than an anytime withdrawal facility. This distinction matters for liquidity planning: an investor must use the permitted interest-payment-date window.

sections.heading: Benchmark-based price
paragraphs: The RBI stated that the redemption price is based on the simple average of closing prices for 999-purity gold over the previous three business days, as published by IBJA. For this tranche, the stated price was ₹14,614 per unit, based on 14, 15 and 16 October 2026.

The formula makes valuation reproducible, but it remains gold-price-linked. Sovereign backing supports the instrument’s framework; it does not make the market-linked redemption value independent of gold-price movements.

sections.heading: Exam takeaway
paragraphs: In an answer, separate three ideas: eligibility after the fifth year, timing on an interest-payment date, and price discovery through the stated IBJA-based average. Avoid treating premature redemption as an unrestricted exit or the quoted amount as a universal SGB value.
